short: CNN-to-LIF decoder (M06) is standard: a 2024 SNN-CNN inner-speech decoder precedes it; 80.13% on the validation subset is not comparable with the 82.6% competition test score (M12); no SNN ablation.
position: The paper [@shalhoub2026cnnsnn] changes the decoder (M06): a temporal CNN feeds two leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) layers trained with surrogate gradients. M06 is standard: a 2024 hybrid of a spiking network and a CNN already classified inner-speech EEG [@sun2024smallworld], so that study refutes the authors' first-use claim (Abstract; Section V), and no CNN-only ablation shows that the spiking layers add accuracy (Section IV). Evaluation (M12) is standard in protocol, but the benchmark claim is not shown: 80.13% on the public validation subset is not comparable with the 82.6% that won the 2020 competition on its test trials [@jeong2022bci], a result missing from Table II. The low-power and real-time framing (M13) rests on a GPU timing, with no energy or neuromorphic measurement. Any advantage of spiking computation remains unshown.
